title: A double-click edits an object's text in acre-gui
body:
Text in a drawing changes only in the source. `scene::edit::move_edits` maps a move back to the source; nothing maps a text change.

## Proposal

- The library gets `text_edits(source, node, new_text)` beside `move_edits`, returning the edit to the string literal or a reason it cannot: text from a `let`, a `style`, a data file, a `repeat` copy, or a node the timeline gives text.
- A double-click on an object whose node has its own text (a `text` node, a box or ellipse `text`, `math`, a connector `label`) opens a field over it holding the raw source string, markup included. A double-click on empty canvas still fits the view.
- The edit is written when the field loses focus: a click elsewhere, or Enter, which egui's field treats as leaving it. Escape does not cancel, since the viewer takes no new key bindings. Jack has not yet decided on Enter and Escape.
- It goes through the link or into the file, as a drag does.
- Row, matrix and table cells wait until hit testing can tell cells apart.
close_reason: Landed in 1903650. `scene::edit::text_edits` and `text_of` edit a node's `text` or `label`, and `lang::string_literal` writes the new string. The viewer's field is in `crates/acre-gui/src/field.rs` and opens from `App::open_field`. Enter and Escape keep egui's focus handling and both write the text, which Jack has yet to decide on. A box without text gets a status notice, not a field, though `text_edits` can insert `text`.
